safety_boundary: Research and paper trading only. Funding or basis observations are not guaranteed yield, financial advice, or authorization for leverage, live orders, credentials, signing, billing, or production use.
obsolescence_triggers: Bybit funding, index, mark-price, margin, liquidation, fee, settlement, contract or API methodology change
material stablecoin, custody, counterparty, venue, borrowing, shorting or collateral change
new peer-reviewed crypto carry or perpetual-pricing evidence
material FX carry unwind, central-bank regime or market-structure change
change to project execution-cost, funding, liquidation or cross-venue reconciliation models

claims.text: A Bybit perpetual funding study must model the documented premium/index mechanism, settlement timing, position-value convention and mark-price liquidation boundary instead of treating observed funding as fixed yield.
Crypto cash-and-carry returns reflect constrained arbitrage and market segmentation and remain exposed to execution, borrowing, collateral, counterparty, basis, liquidation and operational risks.

FX carry and crypto funding/basis strategies share sensitivity to leverage and abrupt unwinds but differ in instruments, rate drivers, settlement, liquidity and tail risks; parameters and conclusions must not be transferred silently.

evidence.claim: Bybit derives perpetual funding from an interest-rate component and a time-weighted premium index subject to contract limits, then applies the rate to position value at the funding timestamp.
evidence.title: Introduction to Funding Rate
evidence.applicability: Primary venue contract for funding inputs, calculation and settlement assumptions in Bybit paper simulations.
evidence.limitations: Contract limits, intervals and formulas can vary by product and change over time; the page does not guarantee that a displayed rate persists or can be captured after costs.
obsolescence_triggers: Bybit funding methodology or product-specific interval change

evidence.claim: Perpetual-futures prices and funding specifications depend on contract design; linear, inverse and quanto structures do not share one universal pricing relationship.
evidence.title: Perpetual Futures Pricing
evidence.publisher_or_authors: Ackerer, Damien; Hugonnier, Julien; Jermann, Urban
evidence.applicability: Theoretical control for distinguishing contract type, funding specification and spot anchoring.
evidence.limitations: No-arbitrage theory does not estimate Bybit-specific execution costs, default exposure, capacity or future funding realizations.
obsolescence_triggers: material new perpetual-pricing result
target contract design change

evidence.claim: Bybit may use exceptional index-price procedures when normal spot components are unavailable, so a paper model must not assume uninterrupted ordinary index construction.
evidence.title: Index Price Calculation
evidence.applicability: Primary implementation evidence for index-component weighting and extreme-market fallback behavior.
evidence.limitations: Documentation describes venue policy rather than realized frequency, latency, manipulation resistance or fill quality during stress.
obsolescence_triggers: Bybit index constituents, weights or fallback policy change

evidence.claim: Large Bitcoin and Ether futures carry is associated with boom-bust dynamics, intermediary constraints and segmented crypto markets rather than a frictionless arbitrage guarantee.
evidence.title: Crypto carry
evidence.publisher_or_authors: Schmeling, Maik; Schrimpf, Andreas; Todorov, Karamfil — Bank for International Settlements Working Paper 1087
evidence.applicability: Institutional research foundation for crypto futures basis, arbitrage constraints and segmentation.
evidence.limitations: The study focuses mainly on Bitcoin and Ether fixed-date futures and does not provide a Bybit perpetual execution recipe.
obsolescence_triggers: new BIS version
material change in crypto intermediary structure

evidence.claim: Published crypto-carry evidence supports studying futures-spot spreads while linking them to limits to arbitrage and price distortions.
evidence.title: Crypto Carry
evidence.publisher_or_authors: Schmeling, Maik; Schrimpf, Andreas; Todorov, Karamfil
evidence.applicability: Peer-reviewed basis for hypotheses on fixed-date crypto futures carry and constrained arbitrage.
evidence.limitations: Fixed-maturity convergence differs from perpetual funding; historical gross spreads do not establish net realizable returns.
obsolescence_triggers: paper correction or retraction
new broader cross-venue replication

evidence.claim: Bybit uses mark price for liquidation and unrealized PnL, while actual execution occurs at traded prices; basis research must separately model liquidation triggers and executable exits.
evidence.title: Mark Price (Perpetual and Expiry Contracts)
evidence.applicability: Primary venue boundary for mark, index, basis, liquidation and PnL modeling.
evidence.limitations: The methodology is not a fill guarantee and does not quantify gap, latency, slippage, insurance-fund or counterparty losses.
obsolescence_triggers: Bybit mark-price or liquidation policy change

evidence.claim: The August 2024 market turbulence showed that currency carry unwinds can interact with margin calls, deleveraging and cross-asset spillovers.
evidence.title: The market turbulence and carry trade unwind of August 2024
evidence.applicability: Official event analysis for FX carry tail risk, leverage and unwind behavior.
evidence.limitations: The episode does not estimate crypto funding returns and cannot calibrate Bybit perpetual parameters.
obsolescence_triggers: revised BIS event analysis
new major FX carry unwind

evidence.claim: Currency carry returns are exposed to crash risk and can perform poorly when funding currencies appreciate abruptly.
evidence.title: Crash Risk in Currency Markets
evidence.publisher_or_authors: Brunnermeier, Markus K.; Nagel, Stefan; Pedersen, Lasse Heje
evidence.applicability: Academic foundation for skew, crash and funding-liquidity controls in FX carry tests.
evidence.limitations: Traditional currency portfolios and monetary rates differ from crypto perpetual premium indices and venue-specific settlement.
obsolescence_triggers: new carry-crash synthesis
change in project FX instrument set

evidence.claim: Continuous derivatives trading requires product-specific operational, collateral, monitoring, settlement and risk controls; 24/7 availability does not remove these risks.
evidence.title: CFTC Staff Advisory on Trading, Clearing, and Settlement on a 24/7 Basis — Letter 26-16
evidence.applicability: Current official boundary evidence for around-the-clock derivatives operations and risk management.
evidence.limitations: The advisory concerns regulated US derivatives infrastructure and is not a validation of Bybit, crypto carry profitability or personalized trading suitability.
obsolescence_triggers: CFTC 24/7 advisory revision
material operational model change

minimum_paper_test_contract.venue: Bybit primary; Binance corroboration only; LBank excluded from authority
minimum_paper_test_contract.instruments: Specify linear, inverse, quanto, perpetual or fixed-expiry exactly
minimum_paper_test_contract.timing: Use completed observations and actual product-specific funding/settlement timestamps
minimum_paper_test_contract.costs: Include fees, spread, slippage, borrow, transfer, collateral, funding and exit costs
minimum_paper_test_contract.risk: Model mark-price liquidation, basis divergence, funding sign reversal, collateral and counterparty failure
minimum_paper_test_contract.validation: Chronological walk-forward evaluation with stress windows and no future funding leakage
minimum_paper_test_contract.metrics: Net carry, basis PnL, drawdown, tail loss, liquidation distance, turnover, capacity and failed hedge rate
minimum_paper_test_contract.promotion: Passing evidence permits paper-forward observation only
